about: Photo look with real Hubble, Webb and Event Horizon Telescope pictures: galaxies and black holes.

image.credit: NASA, ESA, and S. Beckwith (STScI) and the HUDF Team (CC BY 4.0)

scenes.narration: In two thousand three, Hubble stared at a patch of sky that looked empty. It found about ten thousand galaxies.

image.credit: NASA, ESA, S. Beckwith (STScI), and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA) (CC BY 4.0)

scenes.narration: Galaxies come in spirals like this one, smooth ellipticals and shapeless irregulars. Each holds millions to trillions of stars.
When galaxies collide, the stars almost never hit each other. The space between them is just too vast.

image.credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, and STScI (CC BY 4.0)

scenes.narration: Gravity pulls them into slow dances that last hundreds of millions of years.

params.headline: The first picture of a black hole

scenes.narration: At the heart of most big galaxies lies a black hole. In twenty nineteen we saw one for the first time. It weighs six and a half billion Suns.
And in twenty twenty two, the one at the centre of our own galaxy, four million times the mass of the Sun.

image.credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, B. Robertson (UC Santa Cruz), B. Johnson (CfA), S. Tacchella (Cambridge), P. Cargile (CfA) (CC BY 4.0)

scenes.narration: But what happens inside a black hole, nobody knows. Our best theories break down there.
We live in a quiet corner of one ordinary, extraordinary galaxy.
